review_notes: I read the whole file and the dependency definitions liftMatrix, liftGL, glReduce and glReadback in DualNumberKernels.lean. I compared them with Mathlib's Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map and RingHom.mapMatrix. I did not check the other uses of epsilonLiftGL in the repository. I treated innerConstant, innerPure, etaLiftGL, mixedKernel and the other named declarations as legitimate named specialisations and did not report them. innerConstant is just Matrix.map of an algebraMap, but it is used in the file's docs and statements as a named coordinate, so I left it alone. The one finding is moderate. The main uncertainty is whether the hand-built structure is intentional to keep the `rfl` simp lemmas definitional. Defining epsilonLiftGL via GeneralLinearGroup.map should keep them definitional, but I have not compiled that.

findings.problem: epsilonLiftGL hand-builds a GL unit. It is the entrywise ring-hom image of the existing unit `liftGL X` under `algebraMap (DualNumber R) (DualNumber (DualNumber R))`. That is exactly what Mathlib's `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map` does, and `glReduce` in the same library already uses it. The definition re-proves the two inverse identities (`← Matrix.map_mul, ← liftMatrix_add`) that `Units.map` and `liftGL` already supply. It also restates the matrix-map and inverse formulas as separate `rfl` lemmas. The unit therefore has no visible link to `liftGL X`, and the library has two separate constructions of 'ring-hom image of a GL unit'.
findings.proposed_change: Define `epsilonLiftGL X := Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (algebraMap (DualNumber R) (DualNumber (DualNumber R))) (liftGL X)`. Keep the name and the `epsilonLiftGL_val` and `epsilonLiftGL_inv_val` simp lemmas, which should still close by `rfl`. Optionally also state `innerConstant Y = (algebraMap R (DualNumber R)).mapMatrix Y`. Then `epsilon_reduce` can use the generic `GeneralLinearGroup.map` lemmas, and the lift's compatibility with `liftGL` is explicit.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated unit-construction proof. It makes the relation `epsilonLiftGL X = map _ (liftGL X)` definitional and visible, and lets readers and later lemmas reuse Mathlib's `map` API (`map_mul`, `map_inv`, composition) instead of unfolding entrywise maps.

evidence.excerpt: def map (f : R →+* S) : GL n R →* GL n S := Units.map <| (RingHom.mapMatrix f).toMonoidHom
